purpose: Track concrete CGX1 evidence by subsystem and maturity level without percentage estimates.

status_values.not_started: No inspectable implementation or validation exists at this level.
status_values.specified: A repository contract or target exists at this level.
status_values.implemented: A reference, RTL, or software artifact exists at this level.
status_values.validated: The artifact passed its applicable executable validation at this level.
status_values.partial: Some behavior exists, but the complete subsystem boundary is not present at this level.

local_working_tree_candidate.fingerprint_scope: SHA-256 over UTF-8 records relative/path:lowercase-SHA256(file-content), sorted by ordinal path and separated by LF without a terminal LF, for all files changed from base_commit (tracked and untracked), excluding this matrix file.

subsystems.limits: Signed INT8 matrix and candidate INT32 vector operations use the pooled VGPR authority. Floating matrix formats, a full per-wave instruction-issue controller, synthesis, and physical evidence remain open.

Complete workgroups reserve actual pooled VGPR and local-memory resources and preserve barrier membership. A CU-local decoded dispatcher and bounded command lifecycle now connect provisional ring/parser ingress to the authoritative frontend through quiescent retirement in local RTL simulation. Global queue arbitration, public ABI, graphics/runtime toolchain integration, and GPU integration remain open.

Decoded per-wave requests, local-region access, a global ready/valid boundary, writeback, faults, cancellation, barriers, and memory-quiescent release are integrated. The command lifecycle integration bench holds cancellation completion and resource release until a delayed global response drains. The queue path is locally integrated through one CU frontend but is not wired to cgx1_top; ISA memory decode, global queues, caches, MMU, fabric, and physical memory remain open.

The P1/P2 fixed-count concern is resolved at the RTL eligibility-authority boundary: cgx1_tile_power_manager is wired to cgx1_top.tile_enable, derives its cap from the stricter active/requested board state and per-tile operating/readiness status, and cgx1_top_tb validates arbitrary eligible subsets plus emergency masking/isolation requests. Global scheduling consumption of the mask, tile-state sequencing, orderly drain, physical isolation or gating, hysteresis timing, calibrated budgets, and physical power evidence remain open.

Post-decode control supports a 57-bit aligned per-wave PC, live/active lane masks, branch joins, calls/returns with active-frame depth protection, structured loops with call-depth unwind, lane termination, and bounded-stack faults. The workgroup frontend integrates dispatch initialization, accepted-instruction PC advance, active vector/LSU masks, and barrier reconvergence through the residency authority's committed local-to-slot map. C++ and full local RTL gates passed on the current candidate. Opcode formats, fetch/decode, compiler lowering, full per-wave instruction issue, runtime dispatch, and physical evidence remain open.

The executable reference decodes current 32-bit base words and executes the provisional INT32 vector opcodes 0x0-0x7 with 32-lane masking, wraparound, shift semantics, aliasing, and illegal-op rejection. The existing RTL ALU and vector pipeline simulate this same arithmetic subset, but no instruction fetch, stream decode/issue integration, PC update, compiler lowering, or frozen public opcode assignment is established.

A bounded C++ reference fetches one 32-bit base word from an immutable span at a 57-bit aligned PC and delegates only to the provisional vector subset. It advances PC by four only after successful execution and leaves PC/registers unchanged on fetch faults, unsupported classes, or illegal vector opcodes. RTL fetch/decode/issue, other instruction classes, frozen opcode assignments, compiler/runtime integration, and physical evidence remain open.

The combinational per-wave decoder maps raw 32-bit Vector-class base words to the existing request fields and passes non-vector classes through as raw words. Its RTL bench integrates it with the resident-wave vector scheduler and INT32 vector pipeline and validates backpressure and masked writeback. Instruction-memory transport, request identity/cancellation, PC ownership/advance, extension words, workgroup frontend integration, other-class execution, frozen opcode assignments, and physical evidence remain open.

One CU has an executable and RTL decoded-compute workgroup dispatcher with bounded per-context FIFO storage, weighted priority service with aging, tile-eligibility and queue-fault gating, retryable versus terminal admission results, and integration with the authoritative workgroup frontend. The dispatcher arbitrates workgroups; it does not own per-wave instruction issue or queue-context allocation. A bounded C++ command-packet reference now feeds it. RTL packet processing, the I/O-die global queue manager, public ABI freeze, graphics dispatch, multi-CU/tile placement, compiler/runtime submission and completion, calibrated performance, synthesis, and physical evidence remain open.
Architecture targets exist; the global LSU boundary remains abstract and there is no cache, translation, or physical memory backend.
Multi-CU placement, tile-to-fabric traffic, coherence, and contention are architecture targets without an integrated executable model or RTL path.
Graphics, texture, and compression contracts exist, but no shared-machine graphics execution path is implemented.

A bounded C++ reference parses a provisional little-endian workgroup-dispatch packet and reports terminal admission or quiescent completion. RTL locally composes parameterized per-context rings, parser, CU dispatcher, bounded lifecycle ownership, final workgroup-retirement event, reset/cancellation, drain, unregister, and incarnation-safe reuse through the real CU workgroup frontend. The one-CU simulation covers delayed global-memory response before resource retirement and whole-device reset with owned state; the command path is not wired into cgx1_top. Global queue arbitration, frozen ABI, graphics/runtime/compiler integration, multi-CU placement, SRAM implementation, and physical evidence remain open.
Some logical RTL exists, but no synthesis, timing, area, power, floorplan, placement, routing, or silicon evidence is present.
